videos.caption: Keeping your toes healthy is important for overall foot care. Wash your feet daily with mild soap and dry them well, especially between the toes, to prevent moisture buildup. Trim your nails straight across to avoid ingrown toenails. Wear comfortable, breathable shoes that fit properly to prevent pressure and irritation. Moisturize your feet but avoid applying lotion between the toes to reduce the risk of fungal infections. Check your toes regularly for any changes, discomfort, or signs of infection, and consult a professional if needed. #toe #relaxing #oddlysatisfying #satisfyingvideo  #healthytoe

Lemay: Episode 1 of "Elite Technique," my new series made for climbers who want to make hard moves feel easy and look suave AF while doing it. The Lemay is a sneaky lil thang. A technique lost to time one could say... Often described as a "back" or "reverse" Toehook/Heelhook, a Lemay can perform a similar functions as both of those techniques. The lemay allows you to leverage holds that FACE YOU or the direction you are trying to move towards, whereas heel and toehooks are used on holds that face away from you. I'll never forget the first time I saw someone use one to move through a sequence that I had set and thought there was only one way through it... @lucas_oddi proved me wrona and brouaht this move into my world 10 years ago (I had already been climbing for 10 years up to V12 too)! Since then, I have used them as the easiest method of execution in probably 500-1000 moves. At first, my body felt awkward and my hip flexors weak, since I hadn't ever done that type of pulling with my leg before. But quality reps, focus, baby oil, and time allowed me to polish up this method for keeping hip proximity to the wall and adding pulling force to moves! So if you want to learn this technique, I would recommend taking 15-Minutes at the start of 1-2 sessions per week to do exploratory learning and find easy versions; repeat them until thev feel 2nd nature and then make them harder and repeat. Over time, you'll find more and more opportunity for them in climbs you naturally choose. Have you ever done a Lemay? (Don't lie to me... The key to a strong and stable structure lies beneath the surface. Let’s dig into the fascinating world of footings! 🔍 🌐 Footing Fundamentals: Footing is the unsung hero of construction, responsible for transferring the weight of a building to the solid ground below. It’s a game-changer! But how do you choose the right type of footing? 🤔 ✅ Factors to Consider: 1️⃣ Depth of Safe-Bearing Strata 2️⃣ Soil Type & Condition 3️⃣ Superstructure’s Needs 🏠 Isolated Footing: When you’ve got single columns standing solo, isolated footings are your go-to choice. These footings ensure stability, prevent sinking, and keep things safe and sound. 💰 Cost-Effective Choice: Isolated footings are often the budget-friendly option, especially when the ground’s properties remain consistent. Now, let’s talk types of isolated footings: 1️⃣ Pad Footing: Versatile in shape, efficient, but watch out for lateral forces! What’s your preference – circular, rectangular, or square? 2️⃣ Sloped Footing: Less concrete, less reinforcement, and a sleek 45-degree slope. It’s all about maintaining that perfect angle! 📐 3️⃣ Stepped Footing: A classic approach for residential buildings, although it’s become less common in recent years. 🏘️ 4️⃣ Combined Footing: When space is tight, and individual footings won’t cut it, we combine forces! 💪 What’s your experience with footings?
